lotl.label: What's Going On With the Leafs
lotl.body: The slide has become a story, not a blip. Toronto was beaten 4-1 by the Islanders on Saturday, losing its third straight and tumbling to 11th in the Eastern Conference at 3-4, with eight points and six games already separating the Leafs from the pace. Sergei Bobrovsky stopped 16 shots, but the larger concern is the attack: John Tavares remains week to week with a lower-body injury, and his absence left Toronto's second line searching for a center. That is a thin margin for a club already exposing its blue line - precisely why reports say the Leafs would spend a premium asset for a difference-maker on defense. The season is young, but patience is not limitless. Monday's 7:30 p.m. meeting with San Jose is the next test: stop the bleeding, or turn a bad week into a defining one.

lotl.label: What's Going On With the Jays
lotl.body: The season is over, and Toronto's offseason has already acquired a sharper edge: Dylan Cease's shoulder setback now sits atop the Blue Jays' winter agenda. His inflammation reportedly requires no surgery, but his velocity dip turns rotation depth from a luxury into an obligation. At 79-83 and second in the AL East, this was not a roster needing cosmetic polish; it was a roster asking for more impact. The encouraging counterpoint is defensive credibility, with Vladimir Guerrero Jr. among five Toronto Gold Glove finalists. That matters, but gloves cannot disguise an attack that needs more thunder. Arizona Fall League performances will offer the first glimpse of whether internal answers are ready, particularly among prospects who could matter in 2027. Watch the next pitching move - and whether the club adds a legitimate middle-of-the-order bat before camp.

lotl.label: What's Going On With the Raptors
lotl.body: The preseason ended with the Raptors trimming the fat and revealing the first hard edge of the regular season. Toronto converted Nate Bittle to a two-way contract and waived five players Saturday - Tyson Degenhart, Jamarion Sharp, Nimari Burnett, Jalen Celestine and Tyreke Key - leaving one two-way slot open and a roster still built around its established core. Bittle, a seven-footer who led Oregon at 16.8 points and 6.9 rebounds last season, never played this preseason because of a foot injury and may be a month away. That makes the decision a bet on his future, not an immediate fix. The Raptors finished 2-3, third in the Atlantic, after falling 129-125 to Detroit and 122-120 to New York. Exhibition losses do not count, but sloppy endings do. Now the real test arrives Wednesday against Chicago: watch the starting lineup, Bittle's recovery and whether Toronto's new pieces can defend without training wheels.

lotl.label: What's Going On With the Commanders
lotl.body: The tie with New York left Washington treading water, and the injury report now threatens to pull it under. Jacory Croskey-Merritt is out Monday night after reinjuring his groin - a cruel blow to the rookie-season spark who leads the Commanders with 239 rushing yards and two touchdowns. His 11-carry, 82-yard effort against the Giants showed what Washington loses without him, even if that game ended 27-27. At 1-3-1, fourth in the NFC East and two games behind, this is no longer a team with room for limp performances. Stefon Diggs is among nine listed questionable, though Terry McLaurin is expected to play, giving the passing game a needed chance to breathe. The season is not gone, but the margin is thin. Monday's 8:15 p.m. visit to San Francisco is the next hard test - and Washington must run, protect and finish.

article.title: Maple Leafs Lose 4-1 to Islanders
paragraphs: The Leafs lost 4-1 to the Islanders on Saturday, with Colton Sissons scoring Toronto's only goal and Sergei Bobrovsky stopping 16 shots. John Tavares is out week to week with a lower-body injury, while Gavin McKenna will try to shake off his recent benching. Toronto, now 3-4, visits the Sharks Monday at 7:30 p.m. ET.

The Blue Jays turn toward their prospects, with Arizona Fall League action on the schedule as the early offseason begins. The Raptors converted centre Nate Bittle to a two-way contract and waived five players ahead of Wednesday's season opener against the Bulls at 7:30 p.m. ET. The Commanders visit the 49ers Monday at 8:15 p.m. ET on ESPN, with Jayden Daniels taking responsibility for Washington's botched final play.
